This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming
compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Sri.Bhiswadeb Das who met
with road traf
fic accident

. 
2. The petition averments in brief are that:
On 03-03-2025 at about 4-40 a.m. Bhiswadeb Das as a pedestrian was walking on the extreme left side of KSRTC Terminal 2A bus stand, near plat Form No.4,
Kempegowda bus stand, Majestic, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of K.S.R.T.C bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-F-2135 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to Bhiswadeb Das, result of which Bhiswadeb Das fell down and the front left wheel of the bus ran over the right hand of Bhiswadeb Das , result of which Bhiswadeb Das succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
So far, the petitioners have spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards Transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequious ceremonies.
3. Prior to the accident, Bhiswadeb Das was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 36 years.
He was doing coolie work and earning sum of Rs.21,000/- per month Due to the sudden death of Bhiswadeb Das petitioners have suffered mental agony and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.

` 4. The Respondent - the RC owner of K.S.R.T.C bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-F-2135 has filed written statement and contended that on the date of alleged accident, bus was on its schedule trip from Bengaluru to Arakalagudu and the driver has parked the bus at terminal 4, platform at K.B.S bus bay, after boarding the passengers, in order to proceed on the schedule trip and he started to move the bus and when the things stood thus, Bhiswadeb Das was wandering in the bus bay under the influence of alcohol though the pedestrian movements is strictly prohibited and the said place was exclusively meant for the movement of the bus and thus came in contact with the bus and fell down Chandana Das vs K.S.R.T.C on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141534191/
2 result of which the left front tyre of the bus ran over the right hand of Bhiswadeb Das and he succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
The accident in question has occurred due to the negligence on the part of Bhiswadeb Das himself and that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.
5. On the basis of rival pleadings following issues have been framed;
ISSUE 1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that, deceased Bhiswadeb Das succumbed to the injuries sustained in a Motor Vehicle Accident that occurred on 03-03-2025 at about 4-40 am., at KSRTC Terminal 2A Bus stand, near Plat Form No.4, Kempegowda Bus stand, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-F-2135 ?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation? If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
6.
In order to prove the case, the 4 th petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P.8.

On the other hand, the respondent has examined the driver of KSRTC Bus as R.W.1.
7.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent and perused the materials placed on record.

8. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:-
Issue No. 1 - In the Affirmative, Issue No. 2 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No. 3 - As per final Order, for the following:-
REASONS 9. Issue No.1:- Petitioners have categorically contended that on the date of accident (ie.,) on 03-03- 2025 at about 4-40 a.m. when Bhiswadeb Das (hereinafter called the deceased) as pedestrian was walking on the extreme left side of KSRTC Terminal 2A bus stand, near plat Form No.4,
Kempegowda bus stand, Majestic, Bengaluru

, at that time the driver of K.S.R.T.C bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-F-2135 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to Bhiswadeb Das, result of which Bhiswadeb Das fell down and the front left wheel of the bus ran over the right hand of Bhiswadeb Das , result of which Bhiswadeb Das succumbed to the injuries on the spot 10.

In order to prove the petition averments, petitioner no.1 who is the father of deceased got examined himself as Pw1 and produced in all documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.P8 are the police Chandana Das vs K.S.R.T.C on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141534191/
3 documents i.e., F.I.R with complaint, spot mahazar, charge sheet, IMV report, post mortem report,
Inquest mahazar etc which are the material documents to prove the present point.
11.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Manjunath M V, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0011/2025 of Upparpet Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under sections 106(1), 281 of BNS 2023 and u/Sec.134(a&b) 187 of MV Act.

The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under sections 281, 106(1) of BNS 2023 R/w Sec.u/Sec.134(a&b) 187 of MV Act.
12.

Learned Counsel for respondent has seriously disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident and submitted that deceased has sustained injuries due to his own negligence as the accident in question has occurred inside the KSRTC Bus Stand.

It was further argued that even if for any reason it was considered that the offending vehicle was involved in the accident but no amount of negligence was contributed by the driver of the offending vehicle.

The learned counsel in further has argued that the place at which accident in question has occurred is exclusively meant/earmarked for the movement of the bus, but the deceased without taking care and caution under the influence of alcohol entered the restricted area and came in contact with the offending vehicle and caused for his own death.

13. In the light of the argument canvassed by the learned counsel for respondent, if the Police records more particularly the spot mahazar is perused, admittedly the spot of accident is at the KSRTC Bus Stand.
The petitioners have not disputed the spot accident as inside the KSRTC Bus stand.

According to the petitioners the deceased as a pedestrian was standing on the extreme left side of KSRTC terminal-2A Majestic, Bangalore and the offending vehicle came from behind in rash and negligent manner without observing the traffic rules dashed to the deceased.
14. The driver of the offending vehicle who has examined as RW.1 has admitted that at the time of accident the conductor was not there in the bus.

RW.1 admitted that in the KSRTC bus stand there are number of platform and in order to go from one platform to another platform, the passengers has to step down to the KSRTC bus stand and that in every platform KSRTC Department has appointed Hawaldar and in the present case Hawaldar deputed by the Department himself has lodged complaint against the RW1.

When it was suggested to the RW.1 that on the basis of the statement given by the complainant and the employees of KSRTC Department, charge sheet was filed against him, the RW.1 has deposed that the employees of their department intentionally have given statement against him.
The RW.1 deposed that he had gone to the police station to lodge the complaint but police have not taken the complaint of him.
In order to prove the same, RW.1 has not produced the copy of the complaint which he was propose to lodge.

15. So far as the deceased consumed alcohol at the time of accident is concerned, the learned counsel for petitioners has submitted that there is no mention in the postmortem report about the consumption of alcohol by the deceased, hence there is no reason to believe the version of the respondent that the deceased was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident.

Chandana Das vs K.S.R.T.C on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141534191/
4 16.
But if the charge sheet is perused, wherein there is clear mention about consumption of alcohol of the quantity of 143.45 mg/ 100 ml.
Consumption of alcohol of the quantity of 30 mg / 100 ml is permissible and no offence would attract u/Sec. 185 of the MV Act.
It is illegal if blood alcohol exceeds 30 mg per 100 ml.
Hence, the materials placed on record would sufficient to hold that at the time of accident deceased was under the influence of alcohol.

17. The learned counsel for the respondent while disputing the involvement of offending vehicle so also disputing the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and while highlighting the point that the accident in question has occurred due to the petitioner step down into the area where buses are plying and where there is no provision to pass the pedestrian, has relied upon the judgment reported in (2005) 6 SCC 172 between National Insurance Co., Ltd., V/s Prembai Patel &
Others.

entities.text:
National Insurance Co., Ltd., V/s Prembai Patel &
Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, it was observed that "Claim petition before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal is an action in tort and the injured or the legal representatives of the deceased have to establish by preponderance of evidence that there was no negligence on the part of the injured or deceased and they are not responsible for the accident.
The exception to this general rule is given in Sec.140 of the Act where the legislature has specifically made provisions for payment of compensation on the principle of no-fault liability".

18. In (2014) 13 SCC 254 between Lachoo Ram & Others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation,
it was held that - "Simply involvement of the bus in the accident cannot make the respondent liable to pay compensation unless it can be held on the basis of materials on record that the accident was caused by rash and negligent act of the driver."

entities.text: Lachoo Ram & Others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. In ILR 1998 KAR 1934 between Sri Narasimhaiah V/s The General Manager & another.

entities.text: Narasimhaiah V/s The General Manager & another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case the petitioner was a pedestrian who virtually walked into the path of the vehicle and got injured.
It was observed that pedestrian crossing the road at a point where he ought not to have done, contributory negligence can be assessed.

It was further observed that - "There is a wrong notion which prevails that pedestrains have birth-right to wander around the stroll on the roads according to their whims and fancies and that even if they make every effort to get run over, that the vehicle drivers are supposed to still try and save them.
It has been pointed out in this judgment that the rules of the road require pedestrians to avoid strolling on the road and that the roads can be crossed only at designated places.

A breach of these rules immediately holds the pedestrian liable for negligence and if it is demonstrated that the injury of death occurred due to the negligence of the pedestrians, the driver of the vehicle, the owner and the insurer would then be entitled to disclaim their liability."

20. In ILR 2003 KAR 1104 between Koosappa Poojary V/s K.Sadabba and others, it was held that - "If a pedestrian is crossing over a road at any place other than which is meant for pedestrian crossing he cannot claim any specific precedence and the responsibility for causing the accident.

entities.text: ILR 2003 KAR 1104 between Koosappa Poojary V/s K.Sadabba and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Pedestrian has to share the negligency along with the driver.

In the said case negligency on the part Chandana Das vs K.S.R.T.C on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141534191/
5 of claimant was assessed at 25% and of the vehicle at 75%.
21.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is not in dispute that charge sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.

The petitioner has much relied upon the charge sheet to prove that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and since it was proved during investigation that the driver of the offending vehicle was at fault, he was charge sheeted.

22. The learned counsel for respondent at this juncture, has relied upon the judgment rendered in MFA No.2829/2009 between Manju V/s Mathue KP decided on 03.01.2011, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has observed that - "The filing of charge sheet under Section 173(5) Cr.P.,C may give raise to a presumption.
However, that is not decisive on the issue.

If the Court finds evidence adduced by parties and material placed by parties are sufficient to hold that charge sheet filed by Police is a fabricated document, the claim petition cannot be sustained.
The law is fairly well settled that Court has to consider documents filed under Section 173(5) Cr.P.C., in addition to the evidence adduced by parties before Tribunal.

The Court should not be swayed away by the documents filed under Section 173(5) Cr.P.C."
23.
Coming to the case in hand, it is not in dispute that the accident in question has occurred in the KSRTC Bus Stand.
Admittedly, the deceased as pedestrian had stepped in to the bus stand.
Walking across the active drive way between platform in the KSRTC Bus is generally prohibited and dangerous.
Passengers are required to use designated safe pedestrian walk-ways, foot-over bridges or sub-ways as all bus stand areas are designated for the buses to halt.
24. If the evidence placed on record is perused, in the present case both the driver of the offending vehicle and deceased demonstrated to have been negligent.

The driver of the offending vehicle was negligent for the manner in which the bus was being driven in the busy area like bus stand where he ought to have move his vehicle with all care and caution by observing whether pedestrians are moving in the bus stand in front of the bus or not.
The deceased was negligent for having stepped in to the bus stand that too under the influence of alcohol.
In view of the fact that deceased had stepped in to the bus stand where he was not supposed to stand, certain degree of contributory negligence will have to be attributed to him.
Hence, the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased is assessed at 20% and the negligence contributed by the driver of the offending vehicle is assessed at 80%.
Since deceased had contributed negligence at the ratio of 20%, the petitioners have to forego compensation to an extent of 20%.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in partly affirmative.
25. Issue No.2:

It is the contention taken by the petitioners that, petitioner No.1 being the wife and petitioner no.2 and 3 being the minor children and petitioner no.4 and 5 being the parents of the deceased are entirely depending on the earnings of the deceased and that deceased was doing coolie work and earning a sum of Rs. 21,000/- p.m.
26.
It is stated that at the time of accident, deceased was aged about 36 years.
The petitioners have produced Aadhaar card of the deceased which reflects the date of the birth of deceased as 26-08- 1989.

As the accident in question has taken place in the year 2025, it can be said that deceased was Chandana Das vs K.S.R.T.C on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141534191/
6 aged about 36 years as on the date of accident.

entities.text: Chandana Das vs K.S.R.T.C on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 27. So far as the avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, as observed earlier, as per the case of petitioners, deceased was doing coolie and earning Rs.21,000/- p.m.

In this regard,
petitioners have not produced any document.
Hence notional income needs to be considered.

Hence this court considering the age of petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence, takes the income of the petitioner as Rs.17,000/- p.m.
28.
The petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioner no.2 and 3 being the minor children and petitioner no.4 and 5 being the parents of the deceased are the dependents of the deceased.

29. Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as deceased had wife, minor children, parents and they are stated to have resided together with the deceased, 1/4th of the annual income is to be deducted towards he personal expenses and remaining 3/4th is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.
30.

Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors/Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd) it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40% of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

Hence in the instant case as the victim was 36 years the addition towards future prospect should be 40%.
31.

Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.17,000/-, by adding 40% towards future prospect it comes to Rs.23,800/-, out of it if 1/4 is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.17,850/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group of 36 to 40 is '15'.

Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.32,13,000/-
(Rs.17,850/- x 15 x 12 =32,13,000/-).

32. Because of the untimely death of deceased, petitioner no.1 has lost her husband, petitioner no.2 and 3 have lost their father and Petitioner No.4 and 5 have lost their son in their old age, thereby lost the love and affection of deceased.

So far as the quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate,
loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.

It is further observed that the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10%
in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

Chandana Das vs K.S.R.T.C on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141534191/
7 33.

As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lombord Insurance Co. Ltd, the Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lombord Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of filial consortium.
Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and Rs.18,150/- towards loss of estate.

34. In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
 SL Heads Amount  1 Transportation and Rs. 18,150/-
Funeral
Expenses

2 Loss of estate Rs. 18,150/-
 3. Loss of spousal Rs. 2,42,000/-
 consortium, Parental  consortium and Filial  consortium  (Rs.48,400x5)
 4. Loss of Dependency Rs.32,13,000/-
Thus, in all petitioners are entitled to Rs.34,91,300/- and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.
Admittedly the respondent had paid sum of Rs.25,000/- as exgratia payment.
Hence, sum of Rs.25,000/- has to be deducted from the total compensation of Rs.34,91,300/- and thus petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.34,66,300/-.
35. As regarding liability is concerned, the Respondent being the RC owner cum insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
36. Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Since both deceased and respondent had contributed negligence to an extent of 20:80 this court has already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount, petitioners have to forgo compensation to an extent of 20%.
The respondent being the insurer is liable to pay 80% of the awarded compensation to the petitioners.
80% of the compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
accordingly issue no 2 is answered.
37. Issue No.3: In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.

8 ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.34,66,300/- (Rupees Thirty Four Lakhs Sixty Six Thousand Three Hundred Only).
The Respondent is liable to pay 80% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.27,73,040/-
(Rupees Twenty Seven Lakhs Seventy Three Thousand Forty only) with interest at 6% pa., within 2 months from the date of this award.
It shall also carry interest at 6% per annum on Rs.27,73,040/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

Petitioners shall forgo 20% of the compensation amount i.e., to the extent of Rs.6,93,260/-
Out of the compensation amount

, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs. 11,73,040/- Petitioner No.2 and 3 are Rs. 5,00,000/-
 entitled for each  Petitioner No.4 is entitled for Rs. 3,00,000/-

Petitioner No.5 is entitled for Rs. 3,00,000/-
Out of the amount

, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1, 4 and 5 shall be deposited in their name in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60%
of their share shall be released to the petitioners on proper identification through E-payment.

The entire compensation amount is ordered to be deposited in the name of minor petitioner no.2 and 3 till they attains the age of majority reserving right to the petitioner no.1 to withdrawn the accrued interest for the maintenance and welfare of the minors.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
